title: What Four-Day Week Systems Is
definition: Four-Day Week Systems: systems standardizing the 4-day week.
description:
Strip Four-Day Week Systems to its essence and you get systems standardizing the 4-day week. Simple to say, civilizational to build.

The path runs through Future Education & Work: first schedule designs understanding, then system logistics prototypes, then output metrics operations at scale. Each stage has its own physics, its own economics, and its own failure modes — this database maps all three.

Use the ladder: start with foundations, work through the components and forecasts, run every demo, then attempt the compounded drills. By the final record you will hold a working mental model of system hulls, grounded in real research and honest about what remains unknown.

t: Real Research Today: Four-Day Week Systems
title: Real Research Today: Four-Day Week Systems
definition: Today's documented research behind Four-Day Week Systems.
description:
The road to Four-Day Week Systems is already being paved. Khan Academy and its Khanmigo AI tutor bring personal tutoring to millions. Apprenticeship revivals (Switzerland, Germany, US Apprenticeship) blend work and learning.

Sleep-learning research (Weizmann, Northwestern) shows targeted memory reactivation during sleep. Together these programs form the schedule designs foundation that Four-Day Week Systems will build on — the system logistics results, the output metrics methods, and the institutional memory.

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as system logistics research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

title: 2030 — First system hulls networks graduate 100
definition: 2030 milestone on the Four-Day Week Systems roadmap.
description:
First system hulls networks graduate 100,000 learners with output metrics credentials employers trust.

What must be true first: the schedule designs results have to replicate outside the lab, system logistics manufacturing must reach pilot scale, and output metrics operations need a year of continuous runtime. Miss any one and the date slips — that is the honest mechanics of forecasting.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed schedule designs demonstrations, system logistics cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting output metrics uptime. When all three flash green, 2030 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (4 years from the 2026 baseline.)

title: Readiness Estimator: Four-Day Week Systems
definition: Estimates Four-Day Week Systems readiness from component maturity.

Honest scoring is the point: a system hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Four-Day Week Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Four-Day Week Systems operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Four-Day Week Systems installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 64643 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where schedule designs monitoring, system logistics redundancy, or output metrics maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Four-Day Week Systems Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Four-Day Week Systems: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Four-Day Week Systems — systems standardizing the 4-day week.

Phase 1 — Prove (schedule designs): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (system logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (output metrics): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (sector pilots): system hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and workers-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
